rows.title: CT businesses to lawmakers: Don’t touch ‘fiscal guardrails’
rows.standfirst: The CT Business and Industry Association argued that spending and borrowing caps have helped encourage businesses to make investments in CT.

rows.title: House GOP wants constitutional amendment to protect guardrails
rows.standfirst: The GOP also wants a deduction for households with children and a cut in the tax that supports the Paid Family and Medical Leave program.

rows.title: The history of Connecticut’s spending cap, explained
rows.standfirst: For more than 30 years, one of the single-largest factors shaping CT’s budget has been its spending cap. Here’s what to know about it.

rows.title: In CT, budget requests are plentiful. But budget flexibility is not
rows.standfirst: The leaders of a key committee have the same answer for the many CT special interest groups asking for more money in the next fiscal year: No.

rows.title: Lamont’s $26.1B budget plan takes a big bite out of bonded debt
rows.standfirst: The budget proposal could include a plan to reduce CT’s bonded debt by using rapidly accumulating reserves from its transportation program.

rows.title: Lamont’s plan keeps CT budget within guardrails, pays down $500M in debt
rows.standfirst: Lamont’s budget would adhere to the fiscal guardrails and invest in child care and education while largely holding the line in other places.

rows.title: Lamont, CT legislature appear headed for a showdown over education
rows.standfirst: The $26.1B plan the governor proposed trims funding for higher education institutions and scales back a major initiative to expand K-12 funding.

rows.title: Lamont’s CT budget plan falls short of social service providers’ requests
rows.standfirst: The plan lacks the financial investments that CT social service advocates say are necessary to reverse years of financial neglect.

rows.title: What Lamont’s budget proposal would mean for health care in CT
rows.standfirst: Lamont’s health care proposals include oversight of hospitals, nursing homes and drug companies. Changes to Medicaid plans are possible too.

rows.title: Lamont’s fellow Democrats push back on his budget for CT
rows.standfirst: Some Democrats on Thursday took issue with Gov. Ned Lamont’s plans for pandemic aid, education and services for people with disabilities.

rows.title: A tax break for CT residents working remotely for NY companies? Maybe, but there’s a catch
rows.standfirst: Under the proposal, CT residents would get the tax break if they sue New York to recoup taxes paid between 2020 and 2023 — and win.

rows.title: 5 takeaways from Lamont’s $26.1 billion CT budget proposal
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s $26.1B budget proposal includes only $89M in changes from the budget passed last year. Here are five key takeaways from it.

rows.title: What are Connecticut’s ‘fiscal guardrails’? We’ve outlined them here
rows.standfirst: The guardrails are made up of a spending cap, a limit on bond issuances and two programs that force CT to save a significant portion of its revenues.

rows.title: CT lawmakers may have a new option to adjust budget guardrails
rows.standfirst: CT legislators might have more legal flexibility than anticipated to modify a key state budget control and boost spending for core programs.

rows.title: CT legislators to consider adding $13.5M for winter heating assistance
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers will consider emergency legislation to spend $13.5 million to meet surging demand in winter energy assistance programs in CT.

rows.title: CT lawmakers, Lamont add $17 million to winter heating assistance
rows.standfirst: The CT General Assembly voted unanimously Wednesday to authorize an extra $17 million to bolster energy assistance programs.

rows.title: Pandemic put tax burden on CT’s poorest, report shows
rows.standfirst: CT’s already regressive tax system hit the poorest hard during the coronavirus pandemic’s first year, according to a new tax fairness study.

rows.title: Report: CT income tax cuts would slow – not reverse – tax inequity
rows.standfirst: Lamont’s CT income tax cut and other relief isn’t enough to stop tax burdens on poor households from growing significantly, a report found.

rows.title: Disputed nursing home staffing policy will cost CT tens of millions
rows.standfirst: CT owes nursing facilities $55 million for staffing requirements it imposed between March 2023 and this January, officials said last week.

rows.title: DSS commissioner withdraws nursing home staffing cost estimate
rows.standfirst: CT’s social services commissioner walked back earlier testimony that the state could owe as much as $55 million to nursing homes.
